title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Provisions of the People's Courts on Supervision and Inspection Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Printing and Distributing the Provisions on Supervision and Inspection Work of the People's Courts

Fa Fa [2009] No. 31

All local people's courts at all levels, all military courts, all railway transport intermediate and basic people's courts, all maritime courts, and courts at all levels of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The Provisions on Supervision and Inspection Work of the People's Courts are hereby printed and distributed to you. Please implement them earnestly in light of actual work. Any problems encountered during implementation shall be reported level by level to the Supreme People's Court.

May 25, 2009

Provisions on Supervision and Inspection Work of the People's Courts

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 These Provisions are formulated to further strengthen and improve the supervision and inspection (hereinafter referred to as inspection) work of the People's Courts, clarify the tasks of inspection work, standardize the workflow of inspection work, and improve the efficiency of inspection work.

Article 2 The inspection work of the People's Courts refers to the inspection of the implementation of major decisions and deployments of the People's Courts, important special tasks, and matters assigned by instructions from relevant organs such as the higher-level or same-level Party committee and the Standing Committee of the People's Congress and their leaders, the higher-level People's Court and its leaders, or the leaders of the court itself.

Article 3 Inspection work shall center on the core tasks, serve the overall situation, highlight priorities, make overall plans, be innovative and pragmatic, act in accordance with regulations, and maintain confidentiality, so as to achieve scientific, efficient, and clean inspection.

Chapter II Organization, Personnel, and Duties

Article 4 The Supreme People's Court and the High People's Courts shall establish specialized inspection work institutions or departments, responsible for supervising and urging the lower People's Courts and the units within the court to carry out inspection matters. Intermediate People's Courts and Basic People's Courts with conditions may establish specialized inspection work institutions; those without conditions shall, depending on circumstances, assign full-time or part-time inspection staff.

Article 5 The duties of the inspection department mainly include:
(1) Supervision and urging: supervise and urge the implementation of major decisions and deployments, important special tasks, and matters assigned by leaders' instructions.
(2) Reporting and notification: promptly report to the relevant organs and their leaders on the implementation status of inspection matters; periodically summarize and notify all undertaking units of the status of implementation of inspection matters.
(3) Assistance in investigation: assist the leaders of the court in solving problems existing in the implementation of decisions and deployments; upon authorization, participate in the investigation and handling of certain important issues.
(4) Comprehensive analysis: comprehensively analyze common and trending issues in inspection work, and put forward opinions and suggestions for solving problems.
(5) Assessment and evaluation: organize and implement the assessment and evaluation of the completion of inspection tasks by lower People's Courts and units within the court.

Article 6 Each unit within the Supreme People's Court and the High People's Courts shall designate a person in charge to oversee inspection work, responsible for guiding, coordinating, and tracking the implementation of inspection matters undertaken by that unit; and designate one person as a part-time liaison for inspection work, responsible for cooperating with the undertaker of the unit and the inspection department to implement inspection matters.

Article 7 Courts at all levels shall assign personnel with strong political quality, high professional level, practical work style, and strict discipline concept to engage in inspection work. Inspection staff shall generally possess a trial title.

Chapter III Contents and Methods of Inspection

Article 8 The contents of inspection work mainly include:
(1) Matters in documents of the higher People's Court or the court itself that require reporting on implementation status or need to be inspected; matters in the Work Report of the People's Court to the People's Congress made each year that need to be inspected.
(2) Matters in decisions made at various work meetings convened by the People's Court, meetings of the Party Leading Group of the court, and special work meetings chaired by court leaders that require reporting on implementation or need to be inspected.
(3) Matters that need to be inspected in important special tasks carried out by the People's Court.
(4) Matters assigned by instructions from relevant organs such as the higher-level or same-level Party committee and the Standing Committee of the People's Congress and their leaders that need to be inspected.
(5) Matters assigned by instructions from the higher-level People's Court and its leaders or the leaders of the court that need to be inspected.
(6) Other matters that need to be inspected.

Article 9 Inspection work is generally carried out by means of sending supervision letters, online supervision, holding coordination meetings, and telephone supervision. For inspection of major matters or where the handling status has not been reported despite reminders, the inspection department may send personnel for on-site inspection, or organize relevant units for special study as appropriate, and when necessary, form a special inspection team for joint inspection.

Chapter IV Inspection Procedures

Article 10 Inspection work generally includes procedures such as project registration, drafting and submission for approval, assignment, handling, feedback, reminder, reporting, project closure and archiving.

Article 11 Project Registration: For matters assigned by instructions from relevant organs such as the higher-level or same-level Party committee and the Standing Committee of the People's Congress and their leaders, the higher-level People's Court and its leaders, the matter shall be registered as a project by the inspection department after reporting to and obtaining approval from the leaders of the court; for matters assigned by instructions from the leaders of the court, they shall be sent directly to the inspection department for project registration; for inspection of the implementation of major decisions and deployments or important special tasks, the inspection department may submit a project report, and after approval by the competent leader, register the project. The registration shall include the project number, summary content, instructing leader, instruction time, instruction content, assigning unit, assigning time, undertaking unit, assisting unit, handling time limit, reminder records, handling result, completion time, etc.

Article 12 Drafting and Submission for Approval: The inspection department shall, based on the content of the document and the division of work, put forward a proposed opinion and submit it to the relevant leader for approval.

Article 13 Assignment: Assignment of inspection matters shall generally be in the form of a supervision letter. The supervision letter shall clearly state the origin of the assigned matter, the requirements, the time limit for feedback on the progress or the handling result, and attach relevant materials of the inspection matter. For urgent matters, assignment may be made directly by telephone, and a telephone record shall be made, and the supervision letter shall be sent afterwards. The inspection department shall generally forward the supervision letter and relevant materials to the undertaking unit within 1 working day; for matters handled by the inspection department itself, the undertaker shall be determined within 1 working day. For matters that are cross-cutting or involve several units, the lead unit and assisting units shall be determined upon assignment. When the opinions of the parties are inconsistent, the inspection department shall timely coordinate as appropriate.

Article 14 Handling: After receiving the inspection task, the undertaking unit shall handle it diligently and promptly. For matters jointly handled, the lead unit shall proactively contact and consult with the assisting units, and the assisting units shall actively cooperate.

Article 15 Feedback: The undertaking unit shall feedback the handling result or progress within the time limit determined by the supervision letter; if the matter cannot be completed on time due to special circumstances, it shall feedback the progress and explain the reasons, and the time limit may be appropriately extended. For matters jointly handled, the assisting units shall actively feedback the handling status to the lead unit, and the lead unit shall uniformly feedback the handling result. Feedback from lower People's Courts to the higher People's Court shall be affixed with the court seal; feedback from units within the court to the inspection department shall be signed and approved by the unit leader or affixed with the unit seal. For urgent matters, feedback may be made by telephone first, followed by supplementary written materials. The inspection department shall carefully review the handling status fed back by the undertaking unit; if necessary, it may refer it to the relevant unit of the court for review; if it does not meet the requirements, it shall be returned to the undertaking unit for re-investigation and re-reporting.

Article 16 Reminder: The inspection department shall timely track the handling status of inspection matters; for matters that are not completed within the time limit or where the handling status is not promptly fed back, it shall promptly issue a reminder. After the inspection department has issued a reminder, the undertaking unit shall feedback the handling status within one week.

Article 17 Reporting: The inspection department shall timely form an inspection work report, or refer it to the relevant unit of the court to form an inspection work report, or urge the undertaking unit to timely form a handling status report, and submit it to the relevant organ or leader. The report shall be fact-based, clear in viewpoint, concise in wording, and standardized in language. If the relevant organ or leader requests a special briefing, the inspection department shall arrange for it.

Article 18 Project Closure and Archiving: After the inspection task is completed, the project shall be promptly closed and registered; if it is necessary to urge other units to continue handling, a new project shall be established. After the inspection task is closed, the relevant documents shall be promptly filed and archived in accordance with the provisions on archives management and official document handling.

Chapter V Supplementary Provisions

Article 19 These Provisions shall be interpreted by the General Office of the Supreme People's Court. Each High People's Court may formulate implementation measures based on actual circumstances and report them to the General Office of the Supreme People's Court for record.

Article 20 These Provisions shall come into force as of July 1, 2009, and the Interim Provisions on Supervision and Inspection Work of the People's Courts (Fa Fa [1996] No. 8) shall be simultaneously abolished.
